source_document.page_number_convention: one-based physical PDF pages; printed labels as shown

coverage.other_variants: 603/602 not certified; EC603e legality annotations only, not a full variant matrix

measurement_contract.cycle_unit: processor clock cycle; do not substitute bus cycles
measurement_contract.sampling: Protocol proposal for P12: stage labels describe occupied cycle intervals; sample named events consistently at each RTL clock boundary. Binding to actual RTL monitors remains unimplemented.

events.dispatch_accept: instruction and operands/tags accepted at end of dispatch stage; CQ/rename resources allocated
events.execute_start: first occupied execution stage cycle after operands/unit ready
events.finish: final execution cycle; result available subject to serialization and CQ marked finished
events.complete: instruction removed from CQ in program order without exception
events.writeback: rename result written to architectural register; may coincide with completion or follow in nonflushable writeback buffer
events.deallocate: Resource-release legend shading is transcribed in schedules; exact per-resource architectural monitor binding remains unresolved.

measurement_contract.latency_counting: N occupied execute cycles means final execute cycle index = first execute cycle index + N - 1. Conversion to edge-to-edge dispatch/finish delta requires an explicit no-wait pipeline binding; no unconditional dispatch delta is provided.
measurement_contract.throughput: initiation_interval_cycles measures spacing between accepted starts in a filled steady-state pipeline; completion rate has independent CQ limits
measurement_contract.stage_occupancy: Table6-5 dash-separated entries record stage occupancy. Sum is base execute latency. Nonblocking rows have explicitly labeled structural initiation-interval inference; this is not unconditional dispatch spacing. Table6-6 colon notation remains distinct.
test_preconditions: operands ready or explicit dependency case
specified cache/TLB/alignment/endianness and memory response conditions
no exception, interrupt, misprediction or serialization delay unless explicitly part of case

footnotes.meaning: Branch may be folded for effective cycle time zero.
Variable cycles due to serialization; mtspr(non-IBAT) marks XER specifically.
Immediate forwarding of CR result to BPU for fast branch resolution.
SRU can execute add and add[o] only for the add-family row; Rc forms are not included. This does not exclude the separate SRU-capable immediate/compare rows.
Hit and miss times, respectively, for cache-management instructions requiring conditional bus activity.
Total execution latency followed by pipelined throughput expressed as cycles between initiations: 2:1 means two-cycle latency, one-cycle initiation interval.
Number of words accessed by a load/store multiple or string instruction; add to fixed base cycles.
Variable cycles due to completion serialization.
CR results immediately forwarded to BPU for fast branch resolution when instruction produces CR results; this is not architectural CR writeback.
Numbers specify clocks occupied in successive pipeline stages; sum is base execute latency, not dispatch-to-completion delta.
A single cycles-column entry denotes nonpipelined execution.

rules.statement: IQ has six entries, instruction input up to two/cycle, dispatch from entries 0/1 in order; branch path bypasses dispatch queue.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: An idle I-cache hit returns requested instructions to IQ one clock after request; cache reload contention must be conditioned by variant.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: At most two instructions dispatch to IU/FPU/LSU/SRU in one clock, plus an independent branch to BPU; DQ[1] cannot bypass stalled DQ[0].
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Apply all DQ[0] resource checks; the serialized-and-empty bullet is recorded as a provisional conditional interpretation.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden
requirements: needed FPR rename register available when applicable
if dispatch-serialized then completion buffer empty (interpretation of literal anomalous bullet)

rules.statement: Evaluate the second dispatch after the first allocation; both instructions must obey serialization restrictions.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden
requirements: needed unit available after DQ[0] dispatch
needed GPR rename register(s) available after DQ[0] dispatch
needed FPR rename register available after DQ[0] dispatch when applicable
completion buffer not full after DQ[0] dispatch

rules.statement: A dependency-blocked instruction may dispatch to its unit reservation station; execution can begin when the data is forwarded during the register-update cycle. Second-slot same-unit demand must respect availability.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Five FIFO completion buffers; allocate one per dispatched instruction, and stall dispatch when none is available. Finish updates the existing buffer.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: CQ[0] is the oldest buffer. It may complete only if all listed conditions hold.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden
requirements: instruction does not follow unresolved predicted branch

rules.statement: Second completion is contingent on first completion and type/register-port limits.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden
requirements: CQ[1] does not follow unresolved predicted branch

rules.statement: Retire at most two completion-queue instructions per cycle in program order. Stores, FPU instructions and SRU operations except add/compare retire only from oldest position.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: At most two GPR writebacks and one each CR/FPR/LR/CTR writeback per cycle. Results may write at completion or enter a nonflushable writeback buffer; such buffers drain before exception.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Program-related exception is signaled only at oldest completion position after prior instructions complete; cancel younger results. Finish and completion may coincide in some circumstances, not always.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Five GPR, four FPR and one each CR/LR/CTR summary renames; branch LR shadow distinction must be preserved.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Allocate destination rename on dispatch; dependent reservation station receives forwarding tag. Commit result when instruction retires without exception and older predictions resolved.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: No more than five instructions in execute-complete; five GPR destinations and four FPR destinations in execute-complete-deallocate. Load-with-update uses two GPR destinations.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Completion-serialized instruction waits in execution unit until all prior CQ instructions retire; its results are unavailable/unforwarded until it retires.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden
requirements: FP operations accessing/modifying FPSCR or CR; listed names mtfsb1,mcrfs,mtfsfi,mffs,mtfsf; mtfsb0 omission resolved by explicit Table6-5 ampersand and TIM-FPU-MTFSB0-SERIAL

rules.statement: Dispatch-serialized instruction inhibits subsequent dispatch until its retirement; includes listed operations/conditions.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: isync inhibits subsequent dispatch and forces subsequent instructions to be fetched again after retirement.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: BPU removes foldable branch from stream; taken folded branch requests new target immediately; effective cost can be zero, contingent on target supply and dependencies.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: At most one unresolved prediction. Do not predict a further branch while an earlier one remains unresolved. If preceding instruction changes branch target LR/CTR, wait for target availability.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Younger predicted-path execution may proceed but cannot update architectural register files/memory while prediction unresolved; full CQ eventually stalls dispatch.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Misprediction purges younger IQ/unit/CQ/rename work and redirects fetch, while older work may complete.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Avoiding fetch stall requires branch-specific resources; retain LR shadow independently of mtspr(LR) rename.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden
requirements: conditional counter decrement and CR: CTR available OR CR condition false, and not executing after unresolved prediction
CR-conditional branch cannot execute following unresolved prediction

rules.statement: mtspr(LR) followed by bclr stops fetching until mtspr executes. Source spells mtspr(LK); LR is interpretation of named target register.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: mtspr(CTR) followed by bcctr or counter-dependent bc stops fetching until mtspr executes.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Counter-dependent bc followed by counter-dependent bc or bcctr stops fetching until first branch completes.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Branch LK=1 followed by branch LK=1 stops fetching until first completes; source explicitly exempts bl from waiting for preceding LK=1 branch.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: CR-dependent unresolved bc followed by CR-dependent bc stops fetching until first dependency resolves; sufficient CTR condition can make CR dependency irrelevant.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: IU has one execute phase; while multicycle integer operation executes, another IU instruction cannot begin execute. Table 6-4 alone does not establish exact dispatch acceptance on final execute cycle.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: SRU executes addi,addis,add,addo,cmpi,cmp,cmpli,cmpl without serialization, concurrently with another IU instruction. PID7v overview identifies adder/comparator as enhancement; add/addo SRU forms exclude Rc according to Table6-4 note.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Two LSU stages: EA/MMU then data-cache access. Generic load/store pipeline latency is two cycles and initiation interval one; load miss blocks subsequent cache accesses until refill.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Store results are held pending completion authorization; completion and external memory completion are distinct observations.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: No dispatch if required execution unit cannot accept work because its execution phase/pipeline is occupied; available register bandwidth alone is insufficient.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Scheduling guidance recommends separating CR/LR/CTR producer and branch by more than nine instructions to ensure availability, and promoting legal dual issue; this is advice, not an extra architectural hazard delay.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: Chapter6 instruction cycles use processor-cycle interpretation; chapter6 bus drawings only resolve half-clock increments and defer precise bus protocol to chapter8.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e unless specifically overridden

rules.statement: FPU has multiply/add/round-convert stages; up to three FP instructions may execute concurrently. Normal staged rows specify occupancy; two cycles in multiply stage constrains initiation spacing.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e with supported and enabled FPU; not EC603e

rules.statement: fdivs,fdiv,fres,mtfsb0,mtfsb1,mtfsfi,mffs,mtfsf block FPU pipeline until execution completes and inhibit additional FP dispatch, even where table gives staged notation.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e with supported and enabled FPU; not EC603e

rules.statement: Except mcrfs, FP instructions immediately forward produced CR results to BPU without waiting for architectural retirement/CR update; honor completion-serialization conditions before executing those instructions.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e with supported and enabled FPU; not EC603e

rules.statement: mtfsb0 has explicit completion-serialization ampersand in Table6-5 and appears in the FPU pipeline-blocker list; apply completion serialization despite omission in generic named list.
conditions: PID6-603e or PID7v-603e with supported and enabled FPU; not EC603e

unresolved.description: Chapter 6 latency is execution-to-result availability, not an unconditional dispatch-to-finish delta. Reservation waits, resource stalls and serialization can extend the latter.
unresolved.boundary: Use execute_start and finish with explicit event sampling; do not compare every row to dispatch delta.

unresolved.description: Variable multiply rows give possible cycle counts without operand-to-count conditions in these tables.
unresolved.boundary: Keep sets of values; cannot certify exact operand-dependent timing until primary evidence determines selection.

unresolved.description: Table 6-4 says divide 37 without variant label; explicit PID7v prose says 20, PID6 37.
unresolved.boundary: Use explicit variant overrides and retain raw 37; no exact-mask errata conformance implied.

unresolved.description: Rename summary says one LR, but branch resources distinguish mtspr(LR) rename and branch-update LR shadow; precise allocation/release timing remains to be modeled.
unresolved.boundary: Preserve distinct resource predicates; do not merge both into one resource based on summary.

unresolved.description: DQ[0] resource list literally says instruction is dispatch serialized and completion buffer empty. Read literally, that would prohibit ordinary instructions.
unresolved.boundary: Provisional implication: if dispatch serialized, completion buffer must be empty; preserve literal anomaly and review against serialization prose/schedules.

unresolved.description: Generic instruction-cache reload blocking differs from explicit PID7v hit-under-reload behavior after critical load.
unresolved.boundary: Figure schedules are examples under stated conditions, not unconditional PID7v reload blocking.

unresolved.description: Table 6-6 and generic LSU prose say 2:1, while PID7v overview advertises single-cycle store without fully defining observation point.
unresolved.boundary: Preserve 2:1 execution-latency table and single-cycle-store claim separately; do not change all stores to latency 1.

unresolved.description: Timing table mnemonic/encoding anomalies: mull at XO235, subf[.] omits OE, sc extended field prints --1, and mttb overlaps generic mtspr(not IBATs) with a different cycle count.
unresolved.boundary: Raw table identities are preserved; normalized aliases are lookup hints only. P03 must reconcile instruction form/SPRs against Appendix A and architecture source before decoder generation.

unresolved.description: FP completion-serialization list names mtfsb1 but omits mtfsb0, while prose later includes mtfsb0 among FPU blockers.
unresolved.boundary: Apply completion serialization to mtfsb0; no remaining ambiguity for that classification.
unresolved.resolution: Table6-5 marks mtfsb0 1-1-1&^, so it is completion-serialized; §6.4.3 independently lists it as pipeline blocker. Generic named-list omission is preserved as editorial discrepancy.

unresolved.description: Cache/memory misses, alignment splits, bus retries and maintenance side effects add external timing conditions not fully quantified by Table 6-6.
unresolved.boundary: Table base cycles are not complete transaction bounds; join future bus/cache contracts and reject unsupported test modes.

unresolved.description: All visible instruction-stage cells in Figures6-3/4/5 are transcribed. Source diagram/prose conflicts, truncated tails, and RTL event binding prevent treating graphics as complete executable retirement schedules.
unresolved.boundary: Keep literal graphic stages apart from architectural event semantics; do not infer absent cells after drawing edge or assert replay pass.

unresolved.description: PID7v has no 1:1 hardware ratio, while project bring-up uses one core/bus clock.
unresolved.boundary: Core-cycle timing may be specified independently; bus figures cannot establish faithful PID7v 1:1 behavior.

unresolved.description: n is defined as number of words accessed by a multiple/string instruction; edge cases, zero count and partial words are not expanded into per-operand timing tests here.
unresolved.boundary: Preserve expression plus definition, do not silently replace with a byte-count formula.

unresolved.description: Exact numerical reservation-station/store-queue capacities and all same-cycle rename release/admission relationships are not settled by this transcription.
unresolved.boundary: No invented depth or availability cycle; implementation decisions require schedule validation.

unresolved.description: Chapter 6 prose itself conflates terminology in places (e.g. throughput definition example at 6-2 versus FP staged occupancy).
unresolved.boundary: Use explicitly defined event units and table symbols; do not infer one instruction/cycle solely from a scalar latency.

unresolved.description: mtfsfi row visibly prints 1 1 1&^ without dashes.
unresolved.boundary: Preserve raw value; provisional stage normalization [1,1,1] is labeled, not silent. Confirm errata if exact notation interpretation becomes disputed.

unresolved.description: Figures show younger integer writeback before older FP writeback despite architectural in-order completion/writeback requirements; branch fetch/execute placement also differs from immediate-resolution prose.
unresolved.boundary: Graphical cells preserve source legend only; never bind black bars directly to architectural commit until semantic conflict is resolved.

unresolved.description: FP staged notation and pipeline-blocker list are available, but exact same-cycle re-admission, exceptional-operand effects and complete FP-result/FPSCR/CR observation timing are not supplied by table transcription alone.
unresolved.boundary: Do not turn inferred structural initiation intervals into unconditional dispatch intervals; validate normal and exceptional mode conditions against reviewed FP implementation/architecture contracts.

unresolved.description: Figure6-5 instruction11 fsub visibly shows only two execute cycles (9,10) before writeback at11, unlike Table6-5 fsub [1,1,1]. Figure6-5 prose also says two instructions dispatch in cycle0 while graphic shows fetch in cycle0.
unresolved.boundary: Retain graphic and prose coordinates; label discrepancy instead of extending gray bar or shifting all source cycles.

unresolved.description: Figure6-3 instruction9 add has two consecutive dispatch-colored cells (5,6), consistent with source discussion of waiting for IU. This is not evidence of two accepted dispatches.
unresolved.boundary: A repeated graphical dispatch stage means occupancy/wait unless monitor binding establishes acceptance; no double CQ allocation.
